protocol.instrument_name: Protocol for Resupply of Hormonal Contraception
protocol.legal_basis: Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Act 1981 (Vic) and Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Regulations 2017 (Vic); requirement of the Secretary Approval: Community Pharmacist Program to comply with this Protocol when supplying Schedule 4 poisons for patients seeking the resupply of hormonal contraception under a structured prescribing arrangement (p.5). 'It should be noted that the supply of hormonal contraception under this Protocol is separate to and operates independently of Regulation 57 which allows for the supply of Schedule 4 poisons to a person without a prescription by pharmacists to allow continuity of treatment.'
protocol.supervision_model: Structured prescribing arrangement: pharmacists authorised under the Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Regulations 2017 supply the Schedule 4 poisons documented in the Protocol; must have completed the designated pharmacist training course before supplying Schedule 4 poisons; must operate in accordance with the Act, the Regulations and the Pharmacy Board of Australia Code of Conduct (p.5).
protocol.scope_summary: Victorian Community Pharmacist Program protocol for resupply of hormonal contraception: the combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP), progestogen only pill (POP or mini pill), combined hormonal contraceptive vaginal ring, and depot medroxyprogesterone injection, specifically those listed in the protocol Medicines List tables. Covers preliminary enquiry triage (age 16-50, Medicines List product, initiation by GP/authorised prescribing health practitioner, GP review within 2 years, stabilisation, continuity of use, consent), patient needs assessment, clinical review, exclusion and treat-and-refer criteria, supply of one original pack (up to 4 months' supply depending on product), communication and follow-up.

steps.description: 'Assess patient needs to determine whether resupply is safe and appropriate: Review MHR, where possible/available; Check adherence - has the patient previously been prescribed a hormonal contraceptive on the protocol Medicines List by their GP or an authorised prescribing health practitioner, and are they stabilised on this treatment (e.g. recent pharmacy dispensing history). This protocol allows for one variation in adherence (i.e. the break of up to 4 weeks in the last 30 days for the OCP and vaginal ring) provided there is concurrent referral to the GP for review; Check satisfaction with current hormonal contraceptive; offer contraceptive counselling to explore other options as appropriate, e.g. LARCs; Provide sexual and reproductive health counselling, as needed.' 'Resupply is not considered safe or appropriate' -> 'Refer to General Practitioner'; 'Resupply is assessed as safe and appropriate' -> continue.

gates.criterion: Resupply is assessed as safe and appropriate after reviewing MHR (where possible/available), adherence, satisfaction and counselling needs

steps.description: 'Conduct clinical review': Current medications; Medication allergies and/or adverse effects, including with hormonal contraceptive; Changes in bleeding patterns; Changes in health that would be a contraindication to ongoing use, e.g. angina, heart attack, stroke/TIA, breast cancer, liver disease, DVT/PE, migraine with aura, new headaches, increased VTE risk (e.g. recent major surgery); Smoking/vaping status; Where clinically relevant, measure or review changes in BP. BP should be measured at least annually. Measurements taken within the last 12 months are acceptable where the patient's health status has not changed; Where clinically relevant, review BMI (measure height and weight as necessary). BMI should be measured at least annually. Weight measurements taken within the last 12 months are acceptable where the patient's health status has not changed; Confirm hormonal contraceptive is still appropriate and meeting patient's needs, considering: Contraindications, Medication interactions, Pregnancy and lactation, Potential pregnancy.

'5. Confirm hormonal contraception resupply and plan are appropriate - Pharmacists must consult the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook and other relevant references to confirm the hormonal contraceptive is appropriate for the patient, including for: Contraindications and precautions; Medication interactions; Possible pregnancy or lactation.' '5.1 Excluding pregnancy - If the patient has been using the hormonal contraception consistently and reliably, they can be reasonably assumed not to be pregnant. However, if the patient has not been using the method reliably and consistently and has had unprotected sex, then there is a risk of pregnancy. Pharmacists should take all reasonable steps and assessment to exclude pregnancy before resupply of hormonal contraception. Otherwise, the patient should be referred to a medical practitioner (or other authorised prescribing health practitioner) for assessment, pregnancy testing, and advice regarding ongoing contraception. Note that pregnancy tests can give a false negative result if unprotected sex was less than 21 days earlier.'

gates.criterion: Pregnancy reasonably excluded: hormonal contraception used consistently and reliably, or all reasonable steps and assessment to exclude pregnancy taken

steps.description: 'Do any of the following exclusion criteria apply?' (EXC-1 to EXC-4). Yes -> 'Immediate referral to General Practitioner'. No -> continue to PW-1-S14.

gates.criterion: None of the exclusion criteria EXC-1 to EXC-4 apply

steps.description: 'Do any of the following 'treat and refer' criteria apply?' - STI screening is indicated; CST is indicated; Possibility of reproductive coercion, sexual abuse or sexual violence. Yes -> 'Treat and concurrently refer to GP' ('Hormonal contraceptive may still be resupplied by the pharmacist, but concurrent referral to a GP is required'). No -> 'No: continue on page 10' -> PW-2-S1.

gates.criterion: No 'treat and refer' criterion applies (no STI screening indication, no CST indication, no possibility of reproductive coercion/sexual abuse/sexual violence)

steps.description: 'If appropriate, resupply per structured protocol and dispense hormonal contraceptive: - Provide one original pack (up to 4 months' supply depending on product). Note: supply under the Program protocol does NOT include supply provided under Regulation 57.' 'Where applicable: A pharmacist with suitable premises and competency in administration of deep IM injection may administer depot medroxyprogesterone. Otherwise refer the patient to their GP or relevant health care professional for deep IM administration.' The Program authorises the resupply of four types of hormonal contraception: the combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP), progestogen only pill (POP or mini pill), combined hormonal contraceptive vaginal ring, and depot medroxyprogesterone injection, specifically those that are listed in the protocol Medicines List tables (pages 19-20).

'Communicate agreed plan to resupply hormonal contraception: - Offer general advice about hormonal contraceptive as needed - patient resources/information, reminder of adverse effects - Provide copy of record of service to patient and their GP (with patient consent) - Communicate with other health practitioners (if required) - Reminder that review by GP or authorised prescribing health practitioner is required to occur at least every 2 years'.
'Complete any other clinical documentation required for consultation.' See '3. Clinical Documentation Requirements' (page 11).

'7. Communicate agreed plan for hormonal contraception resupply' - Comprehensive advice and counselling (including supporting written information when required) as per the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook, UKMEC, and other relevant references, should be provided to the patient regarding: Individual product and medicine use; Managing deviations from the intended schedule of their contraceptive method e.g., missed pills/administration and emergency contraception options available if required; How to manage adverse effects; When to seek further care and/or treatment - The signs of VTE and what to do if it is suspected; The importance of reporting new or worsening mood-related symptoms to the pharmacist and usual medical practitioner.

provenance.section_heading: 7. Communicate agreed plan for hormonal contraception resupply

steps.description: '8. Follow up - Pharmacists should advise the patient that they can seek a resupply of their hormonal contraceptive at the pharmacy when they next need a replacement pack or injection. It is recommended that the patient's BP should be monitored at 12 monthly intervals (where clinically relevant). Patients are required to review their hormonal contraception with their GP or authorised prescribing health practitioner at least every 2 years.'

review_followup.what: Patients are required to review their hormonal contraception with their GP or authorised prescribing health practitioner at least every 2 years (also given as a reminder when communicating the resupply plan).
It is recommended that the patient's BP should be monitored at 12 monthly intervals (where clinically relevant).

BP should be measured at least annually (measurements taken within the last 12 months are acceptable where the patient's health status has not changed); BMI should be measured at least annually (weight measurements taken within the last 12 months are acceptable where the patient's health status has not changed).

review_followup.when: When the patient next needs a replacement pack or injection
review_followup.what: Pharmacists should advise the patient that they can seek a resupply of their hormonal contraceptive at the pharmacy when they next need a replacement pack or injection.

review_followup.when: Before supply when pregnancy cannot be reasonably excluded
review_followup.what: Consider the need for emergency contraception and/or testing to exclude pregnancy (note: pregnancy tests can give a false negative result if unprotected sex was less than 21 days earlier).

conditions: The pharmacist must share a copy of the record of the service with the patient and, if the patient consents, with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one.

The pharmacist must make a record in the pharmacy software and an IT system approved by the Victorian Department of Health, regarding the supply. This record must be made available to the Department on request.
'Pharmacists should consider whether there may be child protection concerns relating to a request for contraception and report to Child Protection accordingly.' (conditional)

open_questions.topic: COCP table columns did not fully extract (estrogen dose cells)
open_questions.observed: In the 'Combined oral contraceptive pills (COCP)' table (page 19) several rows extracted with only a progestogen dose and brand names, with no estrogen dose cell: rows for drospirenone 3000 (Bella, Brooke, Rosie, Yana, Yaz), desogestrel 150 (Madeline, Marvelon), dienogest 2000 (Valette), drospirenone 3000 (Brooklynn, Isabelle, Petibelle, Rosalee, Yasmin, Yelena), gestodene 75 (Minulet), norethisterone 500 (Brevinor, Norimin) and norethisterone 1000 (Brevinor-1, Norimin-1, Pirmella). Rows that did extract both columns: ethinylestradiol 20 + levonorgestrel 100, estradiol 1500 + nomegestrol 2500, ethinylestradiol 30 + levonorgestrel 150, ethinylestradiol 35 + cyproterone 2000, estetrol 14200 (14.2 mg) + drospirenone 3000, triphasic ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel phases and quadriphasic estradiol valerate/dienogest phases.
open_questions.why_unclear: Table cell (likely merged) did not survive text extraction; the estrogen component of the affected rows (ethinylestradiol in the low-dose and standard-dose blocks) is not transcribed because it is not visible in the text. Rows marked confidence 'unclear' rather than inferring the merged value.

open_questions.topic: Break-in-use boundary wording differs between flowchart and referral list
open_questions.observed: Page 7 flowchart: continuous use = 'Without a break, OR Had a break of less than 2 weeks during the preceding 30 days', with a break of '2-4 weeks' handled as one month supply plus GP referral and 'more than 4 weeks' as not eligible. Page 17 referral list: 'Has had a break of more than 2 weeks in the preceding 30 days ... if the OCP or vaginal ring is their current form' with sub-bullets for 'between 2 and 4 weeks' and 'more than 4 weeks'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Both readings recorded; boundary at exactly 2 weeks is covered differently in the two passages ('less than 2 weeks' vs 'more than 2 weeks').

open_questions.observed: 'Is the patient aged 16-50 years?' (page 6) and 'The patient is younger than 16 or over 50 years of age' (page 17) together imply 16 and 50 are inclusive, but no explicit inclusive/exclusive statement is printed at page 6.
open_questions.why_unclear: Boundary inclusivity inferred only indirectly; recorded as min 16 / max 50 as printed.

open_questions.observed: Referral destinations/criteria appear from page 6 (flowchart) through page 17 ('Refer the person to GP when:') and page 21 (seek further care); the shared provenance object for the referral block uses the first page (6).
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec allows one shared provenance for the block; range recorded here.

open_questions.topic: Route and dosing fields absent from the Medicines list tables
open_questions.observed: The Medicines List tables (pages 19-20) print hormone doses and brand examples only; no dose, frequency or duration is printed for resupply rows. Route recorded from product class wording ('oral formulations', 'POP oral contraception', 'vaginal ring', 'deep IM injection'); the ring row itself lists only etonogestrel + ethinylestradiol with brand NuvaRing and no dose or dosing interval.
open_questions.why_unclear: No dosing instructions exist in the source; fields left empty rather than inferred.

open_questions.topic: Qlaira and Slinda brand names extract with letter spacing
open_questions.observed: Brand names printed in the extraction as 'Q l a i r a' and 'S l i n d a'; treated as Qlaira and Slinda for readability, with the printed spacing noted.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Where the protocol indicates to "Refer to General Practitioner", the Pharmacist may refer to a medical practitioner or other authorised prescribing health practitioner as clinically appropriate.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Referral destination flexibility is left to clinical judgement; local policy must define acceptable recipients before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Requirement that pharmacists have completed the designated pharmacist training course before supplying Schedule 4 poisons.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Eligibility to use the protocol depends on a training-completion record that must be verified per pharmacist.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'the supply of hormonal contraception under this Protocol is separate to and operates independently of Regulation 57' - distinguishing Program supply from Regulation 57 supply.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Local dispensing and recording process must keep the two supply pathways separate; confirm configuration.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Pharmacists are also expected to exercise professional judgment in adapting treatment guidelines to presenting circumstances.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Open-ended professional judgement clause needs a local policy boundary for an automated rules engine.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'A pharmacist with suitable premises and competency in administration of deep IM injection may administer depot medroxyprogesterone. Otherwise refer the patient to their GP or relevant health care professional for deep IM administration.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: 'Suitable premises and competency' is not defined in the protocol; local policy must confirm who may administer depot injections.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Provide one original pack (up to 4 months' supply depending on product)' and 'Note: supply under the Program protocol does NOT include supply provided under Regulation 57'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Which products permit 4 months' supply is left to the product; confirm per-product quantity rules and dispensing software limits.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Pharmacists should consider whether there may be child protection concerns relating to a request for contraception and report to Child Protection accordingly.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Reporting trigger is undefined and the required red-flag action set has no child-protection action; confirm local reporting process and how the rule is surfaced.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Pharmacists providing this service are strongly encouraged to undertake face-to-face cultural safety training' and 'With consent, all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients should be offered referral to an ACCHO'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Training is 'strongly encouraged' (not mandated) and referral is consent-based; local policy must confirm requirements.

hugh_to_confirm.item: UKMEC/FSRH/RCOG reference set used to judge contraindications ('UKMEC 4', 'UKMEC3'); references list prints UKMEC 2016 (Amended September 2019).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Contraindication grading depends on which guideline edition is current at go-live; confirm the edition the service will apply.

hugh_to_confirm.item: BP/BMI recency rules: 'Measurements taken within the last 12 months are acceptable where the patient's health status has not changed' and 'A single elevated BP reading is not enough to classify a person as hypertensive ... a second BP reading should be taken at the end of the consultation'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Measurement and accept-recency process is left to local practice; confirm equipment, recording and escalation thresholds.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Review MHR, where possible/available' and consent covering access to My Health Record for checking inclusion/exclusion criteria.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Depends on local system access and patient consent arrangements.
